documents.title: Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018
Voting Results Along With Scrutiniser''s Report Of The 44Th Annual General Meeting Held On 18Th September, 2026
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Vidya Wires reported strong operational and financial performance for FY26, driven by robust demand in the power and transmission sector and a successful IPO in December 2025. The company commenced manufacturing at its new ALCU Industries facility on February 7, 2026, which is currently in a phased ramp-up period and expected to reach full capacity around September or October. Management remains focused on scaling up capacity utilization, introducing specialized higher-margin product categories, and maintaining a lean balance sheet while managing working capital. Vidya Wires Limited reported strong financial and operational performance in its Q3 FY26 investor presentation, highlighting growth in revenue, EBITDA, and PAT. The company outlined strategic plans to expand its production capacity from 19,680 MT to 37,680 MT and increase its product portfolio from 12 to 20 products.

guidance.claim: Management anticipates a good strong volume growth in the coming time.
guidance.quote: Yes, definitely. We anticipate a good strong volume growth in the coming time.

guidance.claim: The company expects to operate at 100% capacity planned in ALCU by September or October or before Diwali.
guidance.quote: and the remaining 8, 000 to 9,000 tons or so will be added over a period of around September or October or before Diwali we are expecting to operate at 100% capacity planned in ALCU.

guidance.claim: By Diwali, total capacity is expected to be close to 35,000 to 36,000 metric tons.
guidance.quote: So we will be close to -- by Diwali we will be close to 35,00, 36,000 metric tons of capacity, which was planned.

demand_outlook.claim: Industry research indicates a rebound in India's power demand growth to the 5% to 5.5% range.
demand_outlook.quote: Industry research indicates a rebound in India's power demand growth to 5% to 5.5% range, driven by data centers, industrial consumption and the ongoing energy transition.

demand_outlook.claim: The demand for high-quality electrical and industrial winding and conductivity solutions has shifted to a structural necessity.
demand_outlook.quote: As the construction and power sector continue their rapid expansion, the demand for high-quality electrical and industrial winding and conductivity solutions has shifted from a cyclic requirement to a structural necessity.

demand_outlook.claim: India's power generation capacity is expected to more than double from 442 gigawatt in 2024 to approximately 900 gigawatt by 2032.
demand_outlook.quote: Today, the generation capacity is expected to more than double from 442 gigawatt in 2024 to approximately 900 gigawatt by 2032.

demand_outlook.claim: The transmission sector is anticipated to attract investments of approximately Rs.9.16 trillion.
demand_outlook.quote: The transmission sector alone is anticipated to attract investments of approximately Rs.9.16 trillion.

demand_outlook.claim: Solar capacity is expected to reach 365 gigawatt by FY2032 growing at a 14.5% CAGR.
demand_outlook.quote: Solar capacity is expected to reach 365 gigawatt by FY2032 growing at a 14.5% CAGR.

demand_outlook.claim: The wire and cable market is projected to grow from US $17.7 billion to US $27.8 billion by 2028 at a 9.5% CAGR.
demand_outlook.quote: The wire and cable market is projected to grow from US $17.7 billion to US $27.8 billion by 2028 at a 9.5% CAGR.

capex_expansion.claim: Manufacturing at ALCU Industries commenced on February 7th, 2026.
capex_expansion.quote: While we have commenced manufacturing on February 7th, 2026, I want to emphasize that we are currently in a phased ramp-up period.

capex_expansion.claim: The new ALCU facility added some 6,000 metric tons of capacity so far.
capex_expansion.quote: So currently, I mean we are already we have added some 6,000 metric tons of capacity and the remaining 8, 000 to 9,000 tons or so will be added over a period of around September or October or before Diwali we are expecting to operate at 100% capacity planned in ALCU.

capex_expansion.claim: The new ALCU facility introduced several new specialized product categories including aluminium paper-covered conductors, aluminium enamelled wires and strips, PV round ribbon, multi-paper covered copper conductors and copper bus bars.
capex_expansion.quote: With this facility now operational, we have successfully introduced several new specialized product categories, which includes aluminium paper-covered conductors, aluminium enamelled wires and strips, PV round ribbon, multi-paper covered copper conductors and copper bus bars.

capex_expansion.claim: Manufacturing capacity is nearly doubling from 19680 metric tons per annum to 37680 metric tons per annum through the Narsanda facility.
capex_expansion.quote: We are nearly doubling our manufacturing capacity from 19680 metric tons per annum to 37680 metric tons per annum through our new facility Narsanda via our subsidiary called as ALCU Industries.

capex_expansion.claim: Out of IPO proceeds, Rs.140 Crores is allocated for capital expenditure at ALCU Industries.
capex_expansion.quote: Rs. 140 Crores is allocated for capital expenditure at ALCU Industries; this will nearly double our capacity to 37,680 metric tons and enable new product lines.

margins_costs.claim: Full year FY26 revenue from operations reached 18,396.4 million, representing a 24.2% growth over the previous fiscal year.
margins_costs.quote: For the full financial year FY26, our revenue from operations stood at 18,396.4 million, representing a 24.2% growth over the previous fiscal year.

margins_costs.claim: FY26 EBITDA reached 857.8 million with a margin of 4.66%, an increase of 35 basis points year-over-year.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA reached 857.8 million with a margin of 4.66, an increase of 35 basis points year-over-year improvement.

margins_costs.claim: The company utilizes a strict back-to-back hedging policy for copper and aluminium procurement.
margins_costs.quote: To protect our margins, we have continued our strict back-to-back hedging policy for copper and aluminium procurement.

margins_costs.claim: Gross profit margin was 7.92% in Q3 FY26 compared to 7.93% in Q3 FY25.
EBITDA margin stood at 5.26% for Q3 FY26.
H1 FY2026 EBITDA without other income grew by 19% to Rs. 34 Crores with margin increasing to 4.3%.
margins_costs.quote: H1 FY2026 EBITDA without other income grew by 19% to Rs. 34 Crores. The EBITDA margin increased to 4.3% an improvement of 50 basis points.

margins_costs.claim: PAT grew nearly 30% to Rs. 23 Crores with a PAT margin increase to 2.8%.
margins_costs.quote: PAT grew nearly 30% to Rs. 23 Crores with a PAT margin increase to 2.8% while EPS grew 29% to Rs.1.41.

orders_capacity.claim: Total volume for FY26 was 18,024 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: No, volume will be around 18,024 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: ALCU Industries contributed approximately 800 metric tons of volume after starting in mid-February.
orders_capacity.quote: and we have done some 800 metric tons approximately volume from ALCU Industries.

orders_capacity.claim: Vidya Wires is the fourth largest player in the Indian winding and conductivity product industry with a 5.7% market share.
orders_capacity.quote: Today, Vidya Wires is the fourth largest player in the Indian winding and conductivity product industry with a 5.7% market share.

capital_allocation.claim: The company utilized INR 100 crores from IPO proceeds to repay working capital borrowings.
capital_allocation.quote: In line with our commitment to a lean balance sheet, we have utilized INR100 crores to repay our working capital borrowings, successfully reducing our interest burden and strengthening our credit profile.

capital_allocation.claim: Rs 1,000 million is allocated for loan repayment or prepayment to reduce the interest burden.
capital_allocation.quote: ₹1,000 million allocated for loan repayment/prepayment to reduce interest burden.

capital_allocation.claim: Total borrowings stood at Rs 1,456.29 million for FY25.
capital_allocation.quote: Total borrowings stood at ₹1,627.48 million as of June 30, 2025, ₹1,456.29 million (FY25), ₹1,097.11 million (FY24), and ₹971.08 million (FY23)

capital_allocation.claim: Rs.100 Crores from IPO proceeds is allocated for the repayment of borrowings.
capital_allocation.quote: Rs.100 Crores is for repayment of borrowings. This will reduce leverage, lower finance cost and improve our debt equity ratio.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to bring down its working capital cycle days.
management_commitments.quote: And we are taking measures to bring this down to say the levels of 50 to 52.

management_commitments.claim: Management plans to reduce debtor days from the current level.
management_commitments.quote: Currently, we are at 41 days of debtors as of now, and we can definitely bring it down to around 35 days.

management_commitments.claim: India targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.
management_commitments.quote: India targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030 (CareEdge Report)

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
